solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old relative returning next fast time

indicators.note: returning means the old-plus-relative pair is read back to front

parts.note: a nan is a grandmother, an older relative
second means next in line, as in second to none

explanation.surface: An ancient family member coming back home and racing off again almost at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns O + NAN into NANO; NAN reads the same either way, so only the O moves to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A billionth of a second is about as brief a stretch of time as anyone measures.

clue.text: Characters in 'Crocodile Dundee' turned up out of costume

indicators.note: in a down entry turned up means read upwards, i.e. backwards
characters in means letters are taken from inside the film title

explanation.surface: Letters from the film title appear upside down and undressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters in' finds EDUN across crocodilE DUNdee; 'turned up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without clothes, wearing no costume at all, is naked.

clue.text: Opposite of fun getting poorly; happy ending is void

indicators.note: opposite here means turned the other way round, read in reverse
getting means fun takes the word for poorly inside it

parts.note: poorly means ill

indicators.note: ending means the final letter of happy

explanation.surface: A dull time spent unwell, though with a happy ending after all.
explanation.walkthrough: FUN holding ILL gives FILLUN; 'Opposite of' reverses that to NULLIF.
explanation.definitionFit: To invalidate or cancel something is to make it void.

clue.text: Revolutionary denounces art: it's almost instinct

indicators.note: a revolutionary overturns things, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rebel condemns art almost reflexively.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit so ingrained it seems innate is like an instinct, but acquired.

clue.text: Risk extremes of ribaldry in court

parts.note: to chance something is to risk it

indicators.note: extremes means the first and last letters of ribaldry

explanation.surface: Telling bawdy jokes in a law court is chancy.
explanation.walkthrough: Chancery is a division of the English High Court.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chancery Division is a branch of the High Court in England.

clue.text: Last of firemen only uncoiled second hose

indicators.note: last of means the final letter of firemen
uncoiled means straightened out of shape, so the letters of only are rearranged

explanation.surface: The last firefighter unrolls the spare hose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hose' looks like the fire hose but is stockings; 'uncoiled' turns ONLY into YLON.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosiery is a collective word for stockings and tights, made of synthetic fibre.

clue.text: Male model daring to follow a well-worn route

indicators.note: model as a verb means shape or form anew, so the letters of daring are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man posing for photographs is bold enough to take the beaten track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' looks like the man's job but is the anagram signal; 'to follow a' puts the reshuffled word after A.
explanation.definitionFit: A town's principal street is its most travelled thoroughfare, the road everyone uses.

clue.text: Idiot lied possibly in front of boss

indicators.note: in front of means the song word comes before the boss word

parts.note: a Lied is a German song, and an air is a song
a head is the boss

explanation.surface: A fool may have told fibs to the manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lied' looks like fibbing but is the German Lied, a song; 'possibly' says an air is one kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A scatterbrained, empty-headed person is a fool.

clue.text: Large sum of money found in empty seats after dark in clubs

indicators.note: after means the seats part follows the dark word

parts.note: night is the dark

indicators.note: found in means the sum of money sits inside
empty means seats with its middle removed, leaving the outside letters

parts.note: a pot is a large sum, as in pots of money

explanation.surface: A fortune turns up in vacant seats in clubs late at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' looks like card suits or golf, but means nightclubs; 'empty' strips the middle of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Night-time entertainment venues such as dance clubs.

clue.text: Charming Democrat groomed for office

parts.note: someone groomed for office is fit to be voted in, i.e. electable

explanation.surface: A smooth Democratic candidate being prepared for a political career.
explanation.definitionFit: Something delightful or delicious charms the senses, a synonym in the sense of very pleasing.

clue.text: See 6
Get the wrong idea about husband knocked out by accident before girls' night out curtailed

indicators.note: knocked out means removed from the word

parts.note: a mishap is an accident
pre means before

indicators.note: curtailed means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a hen do is a party for a bride-to-be and her friends

explanation.surface: A husband flattened in a mishap ahead of a cut-short hen party.
explanation.walkthrough: A HEN DO is the British pre-wedding party for the bride and her friends; 'curtailed' gives HEND.
explanation.definitionFit: To misunderstand or misconstrue is to get the wrong idea.

clue.text: Reportedly bad-tempered look

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so a word sounding like the one for bad-tempered is wanted

parts.note: mean can mean nasty or ill-tempered

explanation.surface: Word has it someone shot a cross glance.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearing or facial expression is a person's look, a literary synonym.

clue.text: Relish trick with diamonds — it takes people in

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

indicators.note: takes ... in means the word it holds the people inside it

parts.note: men means people

explanation.surface: Enjoying a jewel swindle that draws in its victims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' and 'in' are split by 'people' but work together as one containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A relish is a sauce or pickle served to flavour food, a kind of seasoning.

clue.text: Dare I spell tricky word for shoe?

indicators.note: tricky means awkward to arrange, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone nervously wondering whether they can spell a hard footwear word.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas sandal with a rope sole is a type of summer footwear.

clue.text: Farewell's articulate before performing a semi-rant

indicators.note: before means the word for articulate comes first in the answer

parts.note: to articulate is to say
a performer on stage is on

indicators.note: semi means half, so the first half of rant is used

explanation.surface: A goodbye is spoken ahead of delivering a half-hearted tirade.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Japanese word for goodbye, borrowed into English as a parting word.

clue.text: Tough on horseback being short

parts.note: hard means tough
a rider in the saddle is said to be up

explanation.surface: A rugged rider in the saddle being brief.
explanation.walkthrough: A jockey who is riding is 'up', as in 'Dettori up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being short of cash means lacking money, the idiom for penniless.

clue.text: Fleet Street's last to probe female having left over sick article

indicators.note: to probe means to go inside the other letters

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
ill means sick
A is the indefinite article

indicators.note: last means the final letter of Street

explanation.surface: A newspaper journalist investigates a woman who left after being ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet Street' reads as the London home of newspapers; 'Fleet' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A small group of ships, a fleet of boats.

clue.text: Knowing film for all ages is in dubious taste

indicators.note: is in means the film rating sits inside the jumbled letters
dubious suggests something doubtful or off, so the letters of taste are rearranged

parts.note: U is the British film classification for universal viewing

explanation.surface: A family film turns out to be of questionable taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dubious' rearranges TASTE into ASTTE, and U goes into the middle; U is the UK certificate for films suitable for all.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd and perceptive, a sense of knowing as worldly-wise.

clue.text: Difficult trial

definitions.meaning: hard and demanding, as in a difficult time
putting something to the test, as in trial or examination

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both demanding and the act of trying something out.

clue.text: After hot alcoholic drink take heavy breaths or shallow

indicators.note: after means the breathing word comes second, after the drink

parts.note: a flip is a hot drink of beer or spirit with egg and sugar
to pant is to breathe heavily

explanation.surface: Panting after a warming tipple, or merely being superficial.
explanation.walkthrough: A flip is an old mixed drink, often served hot.
explanation.definitionFit: A glib, unserious remark is lightweight or lacking depth.

clue.text: Work up a temperature in a French farmhouse

indicators.note: in means the first pair of letters goes inside the French farmhouse

parts.note: a gite is a French holiday house, often a converted farmhouse

explanation.surface: Getting hot and bothered in a French holiday cottage.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up or excite people, rousing them to agitation.

clue.text: Underwear starts to give impression refurbished dress looks elegant

indicators.note: starts to means the first letters of the words that follow

parts.words: give impression refurbished dress looks elegant

explanation.surface: Foundation garments make a revamped dress look smart.
explanation.definitionFit: A corset-like elasticated foundation garment worn around the waist.

clue.text: Lie about coach's self-discipline

indicators.note: about means the word for lie goes round the other

parts.note: to rest is to lie down
to train is to coach

explanation.surface: Fibbing about a sports trainer's personal discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-control and holding oneself back are the same quality.

clue.text: Revise order cutting chapter

indicators.note: cutting means the chapter abbreviation is cut out

parts.note: an edict is an official order

explanation.surface: Instructions to rework an order by removing a chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend or correct a text is to revise it.

clue.text: Commune in Northern France making contact?

definitions.meaning: a mining town in the Pas-de-Calais
a contact is a small corrective eyepiece

explanation.definitionFit: A French town in the Pas-de-Calais and an optical glass for focusing light.

clue.text: Secular ritual ignoring etiquette and uniform

indicators.note: ignoring means those letters are left out of the longer word

parts.note: formulaic means following set forms, ritual
form means correct behaviour, as in good form
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A non-religious ceremony that dispenses with manners and dress code.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay and non-clerical, belonging to the laity rather than the church.

clue.text: Falsify composition of a later duet

indicators.note: composition means putting together anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tampering with the score of a newer two-voice piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To debase or corrupt something by mixing in inferior matter is to falsify it.

clue.text: So it's 'Enrietta's turn?

parts.note: with the aitch dropped, Henrietta's is 'er, her own
a go is a turn

explanation.surface: A Cockney-style query: is it Henrietta's turn now?
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H in 'Enrietta signals dropping it from her too, giving 'ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for therefore, used to draw a conclusion.

clue.text: Look younger maybe despite everything

parts.note: regard means look
younger is an example of less, in less old

explanation.surface: Trying to appear more youthful at all costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' marks younger as one example of 'less' (less in age).
explanation.definitionFit: Anyway, notwithstanding all that, carrying on whatever happens.
